markers.reading: Opening aboard Vindristjarna on the afternoon of May 16; the year is supplied only by YAML.

evidence.quote: DM: So we begin on Vindristjarna, floating above the jungles on the coast of the Sea of Storms, the afternoon of May 16th, about 2 weeks, give or take, until Apollyon breaks free of his bonds and rampages across the world.

time.basis: DM states May 16 and afternoon; no spoken year.

markers.reading: The party returned from the Tower of the Colossus to Vindristjarna earlier this morning, about six hours before the opening cave investigation.

evidence.quote: DM: Maybe this morning you teleported back to Vindristjarna from the tower of the colossus, carrying with you a locked book with no obvious keyhole and no clear way to open but that Seeker identified as a manual of golems, which, should you ever figure out how to get the book open and have a few months of spare time and 80,000 gold pieces to spare, would allow you to construct your very own stone golem, as well as some scrolls and copies of some ancient literature that you rescued from this tower.
Seeker: Can I ask Faldrak if he's finished putting the telescope together?

time.basis: Retrospective morning teleport in opening; DM confirms roughly six hours back aboard.

markers.note: The long rest mentioned at u0245–u0262 predates this teleport; it is recalled resource context, not a newly played overnight.

markers.reading: Wellby spends approximately 30–40 minutes scouting east through a vulture before returning his awareness to the ship.

evidence.quote: DM: So after maybe half an hour, 40 min or so, and if anybody wants to do something while Wellby's soaring with the vulture, feel free to let me know after— yep. Wait.
after maybe 40 min you can see ahead of you must be what Kenzo was talking about.

duration.basis: DM first gives half an hour to 40 minutes, then describes roughly 40 minutes of actual scouting.

markers.reading: Wellby’s awareness returns from the vulture at about three in the afternoon.

evidence.quote: So it's now about 3 in the afternoon, as Wellby's mind returns, as he's reported on this.

time.basis: Explicit DM clock for the completed scouting report.

markers.reading: The ship travels east towards Canopy: DM narrates one hour and then another, reaching a few miles short in late evening; Delwath later calls this the same hour-and-a-half journey. The elapsed duration is unresolved.

evidence.quote: an hour passes and the sun begins to sink.

DM: Late evening, you can see the the ocean, the— see here, here's our sort of jungle canopy view. The, the ocean to your left, the cliffs rising— sorry, the ocean to your right, the cliffs rising to the left. And after another hour of travel, you can now see in the distance this massive tree, with vines, these these vines seeming to climb and and crawl all over it. Still a few miles away.
Delwath: It took us an hour and a half to fly over here, so we took a short rest.

time.basis: DM places the approach after the narrated journey in late evening.

markers.note: This completes the approach journey only, not arrival by every character at Canopy’s roots. The two elapsed readings are retained without choosing a numeric duration.

markers.reading: The party is credited a completed short rest during the ship journey towards Canopy, with hit-die healing and restored ki.

evidence.quote: Kenzo: Good idea, I do that.
Delwath: So we're there, we're about a mile away. We took a short rest, so take a short rest.
Delwath: It took us an hour and a half to fly over here, so we took a short rest.

duration.basis: Established short rest; one-hour short-rest convention, credited retrospectively within travel.

yamlCheck.dateAnchor: May 16 is spoken at t01; 1749 is YAML-derived. The retrospectively dated morning return and the afternoon-to-evening current action fit that one civil day.
yamlCheck.explanation: Play runs from the afternoon cave investigation to evening scouting at Canopy, with an earlier same-day return recalled. No current-play overnight occurs; closing sleep remarks address the players. The travel-duration disagreement does not contradict the one-day span.
